accuracy.evidence: Word sets follow the Common Core Language standards cited by the topic: L.K.5d (walk, march, strut, prance: verbs for the same general action, acted out), L.1.5d (look, peek, glance, stare, glare; large, gigantic), L.2.5b (toss, throw, hurl; thin, slender, skinny, scrawny) and L.3.5c (knew, believed, suspected, heard, wondered: degrees of certainty). Each order was checked against Merriam-Webster and Cambridge learner definitions: damp < wet < soaked, warm < hot < scorching, big < huge < gigantic, glance = quick look, glare = angry look, hurl = throw with great force.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented vocabulary slips: synonyms treated as exact swaps (prediction 'damp and soaked mean the same', 'the mouse stomped' gap feedback), confusing manner verbs (glance vs stare vs glare, nibble vs gobble vs sip), thinking a longer word is always stronger (huge placed above gigantic gets 'weaker than that, move it down'), and reading 'think' as sure as 'know' (sure-o-meter feedback 'less sure than that, listen to the doing word').

lab_distinct.evidence: Each step acts out its shade: walkers whose speed, bounce and footprint spacing show tiptoe, march and sprint; a strength staircase whose picture grows rung by rung; a pull-back throw whose power decides whether it was a toss, throw or hurl; sentence gaps whose clue words pick the verb; and a sure-o-meter for know/think/wonder. Passed the 30% shingle gate, and no other flagship has a power-to-word throw or a manner-animation matcher.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers before being told: they watch the walkers and infer the verb from the motion, feel the toss/throw/hurl difference through drag length (a too-hard pull is labelled 'That was a hurl: too hard'), then apply shades to context in sentences, and finally meet certainty verbs. Step summaries name the rule only after the task is done.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Damp and soaked both mean wet. Do they mean the same? Yes, just the same' (the ladder then puts them on different stairs), and 'A tiny mouse runs across the floor: stomped or scurried?' (stomped is rejected with 'Stomp is heavy and loud').

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve distinct m= messages naming each slip: warm is only a bit hot, hot is in the middle, tiptoe is quiet, skipping is light, a toss is soft, drop is not a throw, gobble is big bites, gulp is for swallows, think is fairly sure, wonder is not sure, small vs tiny, big is the opposite end.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores 0.4 against the family kid limit of 5.0 and adult text 9.0 against 10.0 (learn/readability.py). Canvas words are single verbs or adjectives in large bold type; instructions are one short line; certainty cards are short everyday sentences ('I think it will rain.').

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and 12% duplicate gate. Kid paragraphs each add one shade type (manner verbs, intensity adjectives, throw/eat verbs, choosing by context); adult paragraphs give the grade-by-grade standards, manner vs intensity and semantic gradients, named mistakes, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Checked all steps at 360 px light and iPhone 13 dark (shot.cjs): three lanes, the staircase, the throw pitch, the sentence gap and the three-zone meter fit without clipping; certainty sentences stack one per row on phones; word tiles are full-width thirds about 45 px tall and the button pad below gives large tap targets.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: every task completes with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag has a button route (pick a word, then a walker, stair, gap or meter zone; Soft, Medium and Very hard throw buttons). The walker animation stops under reduced motion and still shows footprint spacing; the canvas aria-label restates each task and result.
